name: Salt Lake City
operatingHours: TRAX (Blue, Red, Green lines) runs ~5:00 AM–~11:30 PM Mon–Sat, every ~15 min on weekdays; Sunday service is reduced (~every 20–30 min, ending earlier). The S-Line streetcar runs ~5:30 AM–~11:00 PM, every ~15–20 min. FrontRunner commuter rail has no Sunday service. No all-night rail.
fareInfo: Flat $2.50 one-way on TRAX, the S-Line, buses and FrontRunner's base fare (2026), with 2 hours of transfers; day pass $5. Tap a contactless card/phone or FAREPAY card at the platform validators, or buy in the Transit app; the airport ride costs the same $2.50. Downtown TRAX stations (~Salt Lake Central to Courthouse) are in the Free Fare Zone. UTA has proposed raising the base fare to $3, likely in 2027.

sights.name: Temple Square
sights.note: Ten-acre headquarters campus of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, with gardens, historic buildings and a new visitors' center (opened July 2026). Free; the temple itself is still behind renovation fencing.

sights.name: Natural History Museum of Utah
sights.note: Copper-clad museum on the foothills above the university, known for its dinosaur hall and sweeping valley views.
sights.hours: 10:00 AM–5:00 PM daily, till 9:00 PM Wed

sights.name: Salt Lake Tabernacle
sights.note: 1867 domed hall with famously sharp acoustics and a giant pipe organ; home of the Tabernacle Choir's Sunday broadcast.
sights.hours: Daily ~9:00 AM–9:00 PM; Music & the Spoken Word Sun 9:30 AM (free)

sights.name: Tracy Aviary
sights.note: One of the oldest public bird parks in the US, set inside Liberty Park, with free-flight shows and walk-through habitats.

sights.name: Cathedral of the Madeleine
sights.note: Romanesque-Gothic Catholic cathedral from 1909 with a vividly painted interior and stained glass.
sights.hours: Open daily between services (~7:00 AM–6:00 PM); free

sights.name: Utah State Capitol
sights.note: Neoclassical domed capitol on Capitol Hill with marble halls, free tours and views down State Street.
sights.hours: Mon–Fri 7:00 AM–8:00 PM, Sat–Sun 8:00 AM–6:00 PM; free

sights.name: Salt Lake Temple
sights.note: The six-spired granite temple that took 40 years to build. Closed for seismic renovation; public tours run only during the April 5–October 1, 2027 open house, by free timed reservation.
sights.hours: Closed for renovation; open-house tours Apr 5–Oct 1, 2027 (Mon–Sat 8:40 AM–8:00 PM, Sun noon–8:00 PM)

sights.name: Utah's Hogle Zoo
sights.note: Hillside zoo at the mouth of Emigration Canyon with a polar bear and African savanna exhibits.
sights.hours: ~9:00 AM–5:00 PM daily (to 6:00 PM in summer)

sights.name: Clark Planetarium
sights.note: Space science center at The Gateway with free exhibit floors plus a dome theater and IMAX screen.
sights.hours: ~10:30 AM–evening daily, later Fri–Sat; exhibits free, shows ticketed

sights.name: This Is The Place Heritage Park
sights.note: Living-history pioneer village and monument where Brigham Young's party first saw the valley in 1847.
sights.hours: ~9:00 AM–5:00 PM Mon–Sat, closed Sun; village fully staffed mainly in summer

sights.name: Ensign Peak
sights.note: Short, steep half-mile hike from the Avenues to a summit viewpoint over downtown and the Great Salt Lake.

sights.name: Salt Lake City Public Library
sights.note: Moshe Safdie's curving glass main library, with a walkable rooftop garden and city views.
sights.hours: Mon–Thu 9:00 AM–9:00 PM, Fri–Sat 9:00 AM–6:00 PM, Sun 1:00–5:00 PM

sights.name: Liberty Park
sights.note: The city's big Victorian-era park, with a pond, paddle boats in summer, tennis courts and Tracy Aviary.
sights.hours: Open daily, early morning to ~11:00 PM; free

sights.name: Church History Museum
sights.note: Free museum on the west side of Temple Square covering Latter-day Saint history, art and pioneer artifacts.
sights.hours: ~10:00 AM–6:00 PM Mon–Sat, closed Sun; free

sights.name: Conference Center
sights.note: Huge 21,000-seat church assembly hall with free tours to a rooftop garden of native plants and meadow grasses.

sights.name: Memory Grove Park
sights.note: Shaded ravine park with war memorials and a creekside path that leads up City Creek Canyon.

sights.name: Red Butte Garden
sights.note: University of Utah botanical garden and arboretum in the foothills, with themed gardens, trails and a summer concert series.
sights.hours: Daily, ~9:00 AM–5:00 PM in autumn/winter (to ~7:30 PM in summer)

railStations.name: Salt Lake Central
railStations.note: Intermodal hub: Amtrak's California Zephyr (Chicago–Denver–Emeryville), FrontRunner commuter rail to Ogden and Provo, and the western terminus of TRAX Blue Line (on this map). ~15 min by TRAX to Temple Square.
railStations.hours: Zephyr calls late at night (~11 PM westbound, ~3:30–4 AM eastbound); TRAX ~5:00 AM–~11:30 PM

airports.name: Salt Lake City International Airport
airports.transitNote: TRAX Green Line (on this map) leaves from the ground-level station just east of the terminal (exit door 1A); ~20–25 min to Temple Square/City Center downtown for $2.50, every ~15 min. Taxi or rideshare ~$25–35, about 15 min.
airports.hours: Green Line: first train ~5:00 AM, last ~11:00 PM (shorter on Sundays)
